description: Shared Proxmox contract fixture between fivenines-agent and fivenines-server. Source of truth: fivenines-agent tests/fixtures/proxmox_contract_payload.json, asserted end-to-end by tests/test_proxmox.py::test_contract_fixture_scenarios (only proxmoxer.ProxmoxAPI is mocked). For each scenario, 'api' is the agent-side proxmoxer mock input (fed to tests/test_proxmox.py::make_proxmox_mock; the server ignores it, it only documents how the payload arises) and 'payload' is the artifact the agent emits under data['proxmox'] -- the exact thing the server's cluster-scope ingester must parse. As of agent 1.10.0 the payload carries an explicit ceph-style 'collection' flags block (reachable / cluster_ok / nodes_ok / guests_ok / storage_ok / error); the server MUST prefer these flags over shape inference when the block is present. 'inference_contract' below is retained as the pre-1.10.0 fallback: how the server derives the same signals from payload SHAPE when 'collection' is absent (an older agent). Both must agree on every scenario here. Change only in lockstep with spec/fixtures/proxmox_contract_payload.json on the server.

collection_contract.reachable: collection.reachable. Always true inside a non-null payload -- an unreachable API yields a null payload (proxmox_metrics() -> None), never a payload with reachable:false. Stated explicitly so the server reads a flag rather than re-deriving 'reachable == payload is not null'.
collection_contract.cluster_ok: collection.cluster_ok. True iff the /cluster/status call succeeded. Resolves the cluster:null ambiguity the inference contract could not: standalone node => cluster:null AND cluster_ok:true (the call succeeded, there was simply no cluster-type entry); clustered reporter whose /cluster/status failed => cluster:null AND cluster_ok:false. See scenarios 'standalone' vs 'cluster_fetch_failed'.
collection_contract.nodes_ok: collection.nodes_ok. True iff the /nodes listing AND every per-node /nodes/<n>/status call succeeded. A node dropped from payload.nodes because its status fetch raised mid-loop sets nodes_ok:false (see 'partial_node_timeout', 'quorum_lost'). Unlike the shape heuristic (len(nodes)==cluster.nodes_online) this fires even when the dropped node is genuinely offline and excluded from nodes_online -- it reports call success, not head-count agreement.
collection_contract.guests_ok: collection.guests_ok. True iff every qemu AND lxc listing across all reporting nodes succeeded (covers both guest loops). A single node's qemu or lxc call raising sets guests_ok:false; the guests of that node are absent from payload.vms/lxc.
collection_contract.storage_ok: collection.storage_ok. True iff every per-node /nodes/<n>/storage call succeeded. Independent of the other flags: a lone storage timeout leaves nodes_ok/guests_ok true and only storage_ok false (see 'storage_query_failed'). This is what the shape heuristic could never express -- 'no storages exist' (empty array, storage_ok:true) vs 'storage query failed' (empty/partial array, storage_ok:false).
collection_contract.error: collection.error. First failure message across the sections in collect() order (cluster, nodes, vms, lxc, storage), or null when every flag is true. A short structured hint ('node pve2: storage query failed'), truncated to 500 chars; the full exception goes to the agent log, not the payload. Opaque to the server -- surfaced as a diagnostic, never parsed.

inference_contract._note: PRE-1.10.0 FALLBACK ONLY. When the explicit 'collection' block is present (agent >= 1.10.0) the server MUST use it (see 'collection_contract'); these shape rules are how the same signals are recovered from older agents that emit no flags.
inference_contract.reachable: payload is not null. A null payload (proxmox_metrics() -> None) is the ONLY unreachable/auth-failure signal; there is no partial 'all empty' payload to disambiguate (normalized agent-side in ProxmoxCollector.collect).
inference_contract.cluster_ok: payload.cluster is not null. CAVEAT: payload.cluster is also null for a genuine standalone node (see scenario 'standalone'). cluster:null is therefore ambiguous between (a) standalone, no corosync, and (b) a clustered reporter whose /cluster/status call failed -- ProxmoxCollector._collect_cluster returns None for both. The server must disambiguate with its own cross-reporter knowledge (a lone reporter => standalone; one of N cluster reporters returning cluster:null => that reporter's cluster fetch failed).
inference_contract.nodes_ok: when payload.cluster is present, len(payload.nodes) == payload.cluster.nodes_online. A node counted online by corosync (cluster.status) but missing from payload.nodes means its per-node detail collection failed mid-loop (see scenario 'partial_node_timeout'). For a standalone node (cluster:null) expect exactly one node entry.
inference_contract.guests_ok: guests (vms + lxc) are only reported for nodes present in payload.nodes; a node that dropped out of payload.nodes also drops its guests. There is no expected-guest-count in the payload, so guests_ok is derived transitively from nodes_ok, not independently.
inference_contract.storage_ok: same as guests_ok: storage is reported per node present in payload.nodes. SHARED storage (e.g. ceph/nfs) is reported once PER reporting node (not deduplicated) and the payload carries no shared flag -- the server must dedupe shared pools across reporters by (name, type, total). See scenario 'quorate_cluster' where 'ceph-pool' appears three times, once per node.

error_path_audit.proxmoxer_missing: proxmox_metrics() -> None (ProxmoxAPI is None guard). data['proxmox'] = null.
error_path_audit.no_credentials: _connect() logs and leaves self.proxmox = None; collect() returns None. data['proxmox'] = null.
error_path_audit.constructor_raises: ProxmoxAPI(...) raising is caught in _connect (self.proxmox = None) OR, if ProxmoxCollector.__init__ itself raises, by proxmox_metrics' outer try. Either way -> None.
error_path_audit.api_unreachable_after_construction: The realistic auth-failure / host-down case: token-auth ProxmoxAPI constructs lazily (no None), then every request raises. version.get() raises AND the node-listing probe raises => collect() returns None (see scenario 'unreachable'). BEFORE 1.9.0 this returned {"version": null, "cluster": null, "nodes": [], "vms": [], "lxc": [], "storage": []}, indistinguishable-by-value from an idle node; normalized to None in 1.9.0.
error_path_audit.single_node_timeout: One node's per-node calls raise mid-loop while the cluster-wide /cluster/status still counts it online. Exceptions are swallowed per-node in _collect_nodes/_collect_vms/_collect_lxc/_collect_storage, so that node silently drops from payload.nodes/vms/lxc/storage while payload.cluster.nodes_online still includes it (see scenario 'partial_node_timeout').

storage_pool_contract._note: Agent-side prerequisite for the deferred ZFS<->Proxmox join (issue #49, ZFS pool health shipped in agent 1.11.3). Each storage entry OPTIONALLY carries 'pool', read from the datacenter storage config (/storage -> self.proxmox.storage.get(), one cluster-wide call), which is DISTINCT from the per-node /nodes/<n>/storage runtime status the total/used/available/active fields come from. See scenario 'standalone' for the pinned shape (local-zfs carries pool, local/local-lvm do not).
storage_pool_contract.present_for: Pool-backed storage types only: zfspool (the ZFS dataset, e.g. 'rpool/data'), rbd/cephfs (the Ceph pool). OMITTED (key absent, never null) for dir/lvmthin/nfs/etc, so a host with no pool-backed storage stays byte-identical to the pre-field payload -- the contract is purely additive and the field is the single allowed optional key beyond the base 7.
storage_pool_contract.server_join: For a zfspool storage the zpool ROOT is pool.split('/')[0] (e.g. 'rpool/data' -> 'rpool'); the server joins that to host-local ZfsPool.name per (host, pool root). This is the join key proxmox_storages.name could never provide -- that column is the PVE storage ID (e.g. 'local-zfs'), not the zpool name. rbd/cephfs 'pool' is the Ceph pool; the server filters by type when joining. OUT OF SCOPE for the agent: the server adds proxmox_storages.pool and performs the join in a paired lockstep PR.
storage_pool_contract.best_effort: Enrichment is best-effort. A restricted token that cannot read /storage, or an older PVE, degrades to no 'pool' on any entry and NEVER fails or flips storage_ok -- _storage_config_map swallows its own error and is deliberately not threaded through the 'collection' flags block. Deploy order is not sensitive: an old server ignores the extra 'pool' key; a new server reads it with .get('pool').

backups_contract._note: Agent 1.19.0+ (fivenines_agent#156, server companion of fivenines_server#1159 phase 2). payload.backups is the one section OUTSIDE the collection flags block: it carries its own three-level signal and NEVER flips a flag (completeness_score is a stored generated column over the five flags that elects the authoritative reporter; a sixth bit would be a migration + a rollout window). See scenarios backups_ok / backups_storage_partial / backups_block_failed / backups_capped.
backups_contract.three_level_null: Key ABSENT = an agent older than 1.19.0: the server reads 'unknown', never 'no backups'. backups: null = the block could not be built at all (the node listing failed; see backups_block_failed) -- also 'unknown', and never cached agent-side so the next tick retries. An OBJECT = a read happened; errors[] says which sub-reads failed.
backups_contract.partial_read_rule: errors[] entries are {scope: 'storage'|'tasks'|'jobs'|'not_backed_up'|'cap', node, storage, message}. Per-storage entries are LOAD-BEARING: the server's rule for a partial read is asymmetric -- a guest with a fresh backup on a successfully listed storage is fine (evidence exists), but a guest with NO backup found is 'unknown', never 'never'/'aged', because its backups may live on the storage that failed (see backups_storage_partial: ct 101). A 'storage' entry with storage:null means a whole node's storage listing failed (every local storage on that node is unknown). A backup read that fails -- e.g. a PBS storage whose PBS credentials lack prune rights, so the prune-preview errors -- is a 'storage' scoped error too, so those guests read unknown. A non-list envelope is recorded as 'unexpected response shape (not a list)'; a storage whose backup volumes are missing vmid/ctime is flagged 'N backup volume(s) skipped (missing vmid or ctime)'. scope 'cap' means an array was trimmed to its hard cap (guest_backups 5000, tasks 50 per node, jobs 200, not_backed_up 2000) and is not complete; errors[] itself is bounded (a 'cap'-scope 'errors capped at N' entry once past the limit). A read skipped because the block's 30s wall-clock budget ran out is recorded under its scope with message 'skipped: backups collection deadline exceeded'.
backups_contract.guest_backups: One entry per (vmid, storage[, node]): the LATEST volume's ctime/volid, a count, and `protected` (from the prune-preview `mark`: protected backups are retention-exempt). Read from the PRUNE-PREVIEW endpoint (/nodes/{n}/storage/{s}/prunebackups?prune-backups=keep-all=1, a dryrun), NOT the content listing, so a read-only PVEAuditor token (Datastore.Audit) sees the volumes -- the content listing filters backups per-volume and would need an allocate-class privilege. The prune preview carries no size/verification/encrypted; those are a later PBS-native or allocate-gated enrichment. A SHARED storage (PBS/NFS/CIFS) is listed once from the first node where it is active and emitted with node: null; a local storage once per node with node set. Volumes without vmid or ctime are skipped. Sorted by (vmid, storage, node). This is the per-guest signal; the alert is built from it, never from tasks. KNOWN LIMITATION: the prune preview reports snapshot EXISTENCE by ctime, not COMPLETION -- an in-progress PBS backup can momentarily read as the latest_ctime (a false 'backed up' if it fails); the server/PBS-native enrichment resolves completion (#1164). Local/NFS/dir storages are unaffected.
backups_contract.tasks: Finished vzdump tasks per node (limit 50), JOB-level: status is the free string PVE reports ('OK', 'WARNINGS: <n>', or an error message), passed verbatim and capped -- the server classifies it. id is the vmid only when exactly one guest was backed up (pve-manager VZDump.pm); a scheduled multi-guest job has an empty id, shipped as null. Never attribute a task to a guest.
backups_contract.jobs: /cluster/backup definitions trimmed to id/enabled/schedule/storage/vmid/all/exclude/pool/node/mode/comment/next_run (PVE's 'next-run'). Display context and the schedule the server can size a default threshold from.
backups_contract.not_backed_up: /cluster/backup-info/not-backed-up verbatim: [{vmid, name, type}] -- guests covered by no job, the signal a job-level webhook can never produce.
backups_contract.freshness: The block is computed at most once per 600s and re-emitted with age_s = seconds since it was computed (monotonic). Anchor freshness as received_at - age_s; never trust the agent wall clock. latest_ctime and task starttime/endtime are PVE data timestamps and pass through as-is. In every scenario here age_s is 0 because the block was just computed.
backups_contract.no_config_key: The TTL and caps are agent constants. config['proxmox'] is splatted into proxmox_metrics(**config): a key the server started sending would be a TypeError on every older agent and kill the whole Proxmox collector there. Do not add one.
backups_contract.scrubbing: Every customer-controlled string (volid, status, comment, upid, name...) is UTF-8-sanitized, NUL-stripped and capped at 500 chars agent-side; the server ingester applies its own scrub regardless.

quorate_cluster.description: 3-node quorate cluster 'production'. Guests spread across nodes (pve1: vm 100 + ct 200; pve2: vm 101; pve3: stopped ct 201). Shared storage 'ceph-pool' visible on all three nodes (reported 3x, once per node -- server must dedupe) plus a per-node 'local-lvm'. cluster.nodes_online (3) == len(nodes) (3) => nodes_ok. This is the fully-healthy reference shape.

quorum_lost.description: 2-node cluster 'homelab' that lost quorum: pve2 is down, so the surviving reporter pve1 has quorate:false and nodes_online:1. pve2 stays in /cluster/status (config membership) but every pve2 per-node call raises, so it drops from nodes/vms/lxc/storage. Pins quorate:false serialization AND nodes_online (1) < cluster.nodes (2).

standalone.description: Standalone node (never joined a cluster): /cluster/status returns only the local node entry with no 'cluster'-type entry, so _collect_cluster returns None => payload.cluster is null. version present and nodes non-empty prove reachability -- this is the shape the server must NOT confuse with 'unreachable' (payload:null). Reuses the None-return pinned by test_collect_cluster_no_cluster_entry_returns_none (T25).

unreachable.description: Whole-module failure: API unreachable / auth failure after lazy token-auth construction. version.get() raises AND the node-listing reachability probe raises => collect() returns None => data['proxmox'] is null. This is the ONLY unreachable signal (there is no 'all empty' partial payload). Server reads reachable=false. NOTE (agent 1.9.0 normalization): before 1.9.0 this scenario returned {"version": null, "cluster": null, "nodes": [], "vms": [], "lxc": [], "storage": []}, which the server could not tell apart from a healthy idle node by value.

partial_node_timeout.description: Healthy 3-node quorate cluster where pve2's per-node API hangs (times out) mid-loop while corosync still counts it online. The cluster-wide /cluster/status call succeeds, so payload.cluster.nodes_online stays 3, but pve2's status/qemu/lxc/storage calls each raise and are swallowed per-node -- pve2 silently drops from nodes/vms/lxc/storage. The explicit collection block reports this directly: nodes_ok/guests_ok/storage_ok all false (cluster_ok stays true), error the first failure ('node pve2: status query failed'). It also pins the pre-1.10.0 fallback shape for the same signal: cluster.nodes_online (3) != len(nodes) (2).

cluster_fetch_failed.description: Clustered reporter whose /cluster/status call fails (mon/pmxcfs hiccup) while its own node detail, guests, and storage all succeed. _collect_cluster swallows the error and returns None, so payload.cluster is null -- SHAPE-identical to 'standalone'. The explicit flag is what tells them apart: here cluster_ok is false (the call raised), whereas 'standalone' has cluster_ok true (the call succeeded, there was just no cluster entry). This is the disambiguation the whole collection block exists to provide. error is the first (and only) failure. version + nodes present => reachable true.

storage_query_failed.description: Healthy 2-node quorate cluster where ONLY pve2's /nodes/pve2/storage call fails (e.g. a wedged storage plugin) -- its status, qemu, and lxc calls all succeed. pve2 stays in payload.nodes with its guests; just its storage rows drop. Pins storage_ok independence: nodes_ok/guests_ok stay true and only storage_ok is false, the exact shape from issue #80's example. This is what shape inference could never express: an empty/partial storage array here means 'query failed' (storage_ok:false), not 'no storages exist' (storage_ok:true).

backups_ok.description: Reference shape for the backups block (#156). 2-node cluster. Shared PBS storage 'pbs-main' is visible on both nodes but LISTED ONCE, from pve1 (the first node where it is active), and emitted with node:null -- pve2's copy of the listing carries a decoy vm 999 entry that MUST NOT appear, proving the second listing never happened. Local 'local' (dir) is listed per node with node set; 'local-lvm' cannot hold backups (content lacks 'backup') and is never listed. vm 100 has two PBS snapshots (aggregated: latest ctime/volid/size/verification, count 2, encrypted from PBS's fingerprint-or-'1' spelling) plus one on local; ct 101 has one PBS snapshot and three on pve2's local. Tasks: pve1 'OK', pve2 'WARNINGS: 1' (verbatim, server classifies); both have an empty id (multi-guest job) -> null. One job with the noise fields (bwlimit/compress/mailto) dropped and next-run -> next_run. vm 105 is in no job. age_s is 0 because the block was just computed.

backups_storage_partial.description: Partial backups read (#156 rule 1). Standalone node with a shared PBS 'pbs-main' whose content listing raises and a local 'local' that lists fine. The block is still emitted: vm 100's backup on 'local' is present, and errors[] carries ONE entry naming the failed storage (scope 'storage', storage 'pbs-main', node = the node the listing was attempted from, message = the API's reason). The server's asymmetric rule hangs on that entry: ct 101, which has no backup anywhere in this payload, must read as UNKNOWN (its backups may be on pbs-main), never as 'never backed up'. collection stays all-true: the block never touches the flags (rule 2).

backups_block_failed.description: backups:null (#156 rule 1, middle level). The node listing succeeds for the five flagged sections (nodes_raises_from_call=5: collect() lists nodes once per section in the fixed order nodes/vms/lxc/storage/backups, so the 5th call -- the backups build -- is the first to raise). Nothing in the block can be read without the node list, so the whole block is null rather than an object with empty arrays that would read as 'no backups anywhere'. collection is all-true and error is null: the failure is NOT threaded through the flags (rule 2), and store_if keeps the None out of the TTL cache so the next tick retries.

backups_capped.description: Cap trimming is never silent (#156 rule 5). PVE is asked for limit=50 vzdump tasks per node; this node answers 51 (a PVE that ignored the limit). The agent keeps the first 50 and adds an errors[] entry with scope 'cap' naming the node, so a trimmed array is never mistaken for a complete one. guest_backups (5000), jobs (200) and not_backed_up (2000) trim the same way (unit-tested; too large to pin here).
